slides.title: Everything you do is an op.
slides.text: Reading a list, ticking an item, searching your notes, syncing with a friend: each is an {op}, a small piece of JSON that says what to do. One engine runs them all.

slides.title: A simple query.
slides.text: “What's still open, soonest first?” An op takes data, narrows it and hands back an answer. It runs on your own device, over what you can already read.

slides.title: Changes are ops too.
slides.text: Ticking an item is an op. The engine checks your rule, turns the op into a CRDT change, signs it and hands it to sync.

slides.title: Walking a graph.
slides.text: Data links to data: a list to its items, an item to a photo, a person to their friends. A {walk} follows links hop by hop, and stops wherever your rules stop.

slides.title: Searching by words.
slides.text: A {search} finds the notes that best match your words, ranked the way search engines do it (BM25). The index is built on your device, from what you can read, and never leaves it.

slides.title: Searching by meaning.
slides.text: “Plumbing problems” should also find “water under the sink”. A {near} op compares meaning as vectors and returns the closest entries. Same rule: the index is local.

slides.title: Ops chain together.
slides.text: The output of one op is the input of the next. Search by meaning, follow the links to whoever is assigned, keep only what's open.

slides.title: New kinds of ops plug in.
slides.text: find, walk, search and near are {plugins}. Each one declares its name, the shape of its JSON, and which rule op it needs. A new plugin, say for maps or for time series, slots in the same way.

slides.title: Sync is ops too.
slides.text: Your device's sync plan is written as ops: what it wants, what it keeps, what it passes on. Here, your phone keeps three months of the house list and only wants the photos you open.

slides.title: Rules name the ops.
slides.text: Before the engine runs an op, it looks up the rule behind it. A plugin's op is allowed only if the rule lists the op it needs. No rule, no answer.

slides.title: Answers without reading.
slides.text: Some roles may ask questions but not read. A device that may read runs the op for them and returns only the answer. The street may learn how many tasks are open, never which ones.

slides.title: The ops engine, in short.
list: Every read, change, search and sync is a JSON op.
Ops chain: one op's answer feeds the next.
New kinds of ops plug in, each naming the rule op it needs.
Queries run where the keys are; others may get answers, never the data.
